decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents.Drawing no. 110, 111, 112, 120, 150, 160, P26-0030_0012, P26-0030_0013 SuDs proforma and strategy, dated May 2026Flood Risk Assessment & Advice, dated April 2026Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment, dated 25.05.26Biodiversity Metric Calculation Tool   Biodiversity Statement   Court foundationDesign and Access statement Arboricultural Method Statement, dated 24.05.26Public Benefit statement Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Roost Assessment, dated 02.03.26Planning StatementParking SurveySheffield Stand specificationTransport Statement, dated May 2026Lighting Impact Assessment, dated 27.05.26Lighting Assessment -  padel light technical dataConstruction Logistic Plan, dated May 2026Schedule of Materials and FinishesReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance.

Before development commences, a report should be carried out by an approved acoustic consultant and submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval, that assesses the likely noise impacts from the development with regards to its use as a padel court. The report shall also clearly outline mitigation measures for the development to reduce these noise impacts to acceptable levels.It should include all calculations and baseline data, and be set out so that the Local Planning Authority can fully audit the report and critically analyse the contents and recommendations. The approved measures shall be implemented in their entirety before the use commences.Reason: To ensure that the amenities of neighbouring premises are protected from noise from the development in accordance with Policies D13 and D14 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to the commencement of development, a detailed Construction and Logistics Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The plan shall include:i.	A photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site;ii.	Works programme;iii.	Trip generation associated with the construction project, swept path analysis and identification of any works needed to the public highway;iv.	Routeing - primary and secondary designated routes to show how vehicles will keep to main routes and comply with the London Lorry Control Scheme;v.	Delivery scheduling;vi.	Use of holding areas and vehicle call up;vii.	Permit schemes and access;viii.	Parking, loading and unloading arrangements;ix.	Traffic management;x.	Details of contractor FORS membership.xi.	Measures to reduce Work Related Road Risk.xii.	Storage of construction materials, chemicals and equipmentxiii.	CLP management including contact details for the person responsible for ensuring compliance with the Plan during construction;xiv.	Provision of wheel cleaning facilities;xv.      Measures to control the emission of dust and dirt during construction;xvi.	Details of safe access for people walking or cycling across the site; access will be provided and maintained during all phases of construction; and Visual screening.The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.Reason: In order to ensure that the impact of the development on the surrounding transport network is sufficiently assessed and where necessary appropriately mitigated in accordance with policy DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the pre-commencement of the development, a Fire Statement, which is an independent fire strategy produced by a third party, suitably qualified assessor, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Fire Commissioner. The approved measures shall be implemented on site prior to the occupation of the development and shall be permanently maintained.Reason: In the interests of the safety of future occupiers and to accord with London Plan Policy D12

Prior to the first use of the site, details of all means of enclosure, fencing, gates and any associated ball-stop fencing/netting, together with details of pedestrian and maintenance vehicle access arrangements to the existing artificial pitches and associated sports facilities, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submitted details shall demonstrate that safe and convenient access to and from the existing artificial pitches, changing facilities and maintenance areas will be retained at all times and that the proposed development will not prejudice the ongoing use, management or maintenance of the existing sports facilities.The approved means of enclosure and access arrangements shall be implemented in full prior to the first use of the development and shall thereafter be retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure satisfactory appearance and safeguard the privacy, amenity and safety of adjoining occupiers and the public and in the interests of highway safety.

The development hereby authorised shall be carried out in strict accordance with the mitigation measures set out in the submitted arboricultural report (prepared by Arbtech, dated 24.05.26). In particular the construction exclusion area as shown in the Tree Protection Plan section of that document shall be in place before construction works begin and only removed after all construction works have ended.Reason: In the interests of ensuring the trees to be retained, including preserved trees, are protected, in accordance with DMD 80 of the Enfield Development Management Document 2014 and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the ecological mitigation and protection measures set out in the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Roost Assessment dated 02.03.2026, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.These measures shall be implemented prior to and throughout all site clearance, vegetation removal and construction works, and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.In the event that, during the construction phase, any part of the site is identified as having potential for roosting bats, works in the affected area shall cease immediately. An updated survey and/or detailed inspection shall be undertaken by a suitably qualified and licensed ecologist, and the findings, together with any further mitigation measures, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority before works recommence.Reason: To ensure the protection of biodiversity and protected species

The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use until the provision of 3 no. Sheffield cycle stands (6 cycle spaces), have been installed in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of adequate and secure cycle parking in the interests of promoting sustainable transport

The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use unless and until 2 no. additional Blue Badge parking spaces have been provided within the existing car park in accordance with details to be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The approved spaces shall be clearly marked, signed, and made available for use prior to the first use of the padel courts and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of adequate accessible parking for disabled users, in the interests of inclusivity and accessibility.

The facility hereby permitted shall not be open to customers and associated floodlighting shall not be used outside the following times:Monday to Friday: 07:00 to 21:00Saturday, Sunday and Public Holidays: 09:00-17:00  Reason: To ensure neighbouring residential amenity is not unduly impacted.

The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use unless and until the pedestrian access arrangements, including the dedicated pedestrian access route to the padel facility, controlled entry point, push-to-exit egress provision, and east-west pedestrian links as shown on the approved plans, have been fully implemented.The approved access arrangements shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure safe, convenient and accessible pedestrian access to the development, in the interests of user safety, permeability and good design.

The development hereby permitted shall not be brought in use until the details outlined in the SuDs Strategy (dated May, 2026) have been implemented. The sustainable drainage system shall be implemented and thereafter managed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use unless and until all external lighting has been installed and operated in full accordance with the mitigation measures and lighting strategy set out in the approved Lighting Impact Assessment (Hawkins Environmental, dated May 2026).Reason: To ensure that external lighting is designed and operated to minimise light pollution

Prior to first use of the development, refuse storage facilities shall be provided and implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of the development, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

open_spaces_details.description:
0.13ha of the site lies within Metropolitan Open Land (MOL) and is designated as Local Open Space. However, in its current condition, this area does not make a positive contribution to the openness, character, or amenity value of the designated land. The site is well contained between the existing 3G football pitches and the leisure centre and is perceived as part of an established and developed leisure setting.

The proposed Southbury Padel Centre will diversify and enhance the existing sports offer at Southbury Leisure Centre. The facility will operate on a ?pay and play? basis, enabling access for both members and non-members. Concessionary rates will be available during off-peak hours to support inclusive community use. Further details are provided within the accompanying Southbury Padel Centre Public Benefit document.
